definition: A family of clinical conditions caused by atherosclerosis — the buildup of lipid-rich plaque in the arterial wall — leading to arterial narrowing, plaque rupture, thrombosis, and downstream ischemia or infarction of the tissue supplied. ASCVD is the shared pathological substrate underlying most heart attacks and ischemic strokes and is the endpoint that primary-prevention risk scores (PREVENT, Pooled Cohort Equations, SCORE2) are built to predict.
note_type2_exclusions: Non-atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is out of scope as a *disease endpoint* but its risk factors may overlap: heart failure without ischemia, atrial fibrillation, valvular disease, congenital heart disease, and Type 2 (supply-demand) MI. These are excluded as endpoints but relevant comorbid factors are retained when the literature reports them as ASCVD risk factors.

prevent_baseline.known_omissions_hypothesis: PREVENT deliberately excludes race (unlike the Pooled Cohort Equations) and omits family history, lipoprotein(a), inflammatory markers (hs-CRP), coronary artery calcium, and many emerging factors — these are prime candidates for the gap analysis.
